findings.description: The new residual sentence claims the policy hook's command escapes the seal: "a hook contributes no tool, and its command runs outside the worktree the seal bounds". That is false for the case it describes, and it contradicts the bullet directly above it. A hook's command is a child of the reviewer's session, and the session is started with its working directory set to the sealed snapshot worktree (internal/reviewer/supervise.go:103 passes `Dir: run.Worktree`, internal/agent/claude.go:126 sets `command.Dir = request.Dir`). Concrete path: a policy-configured `SessionStart` hook running `mkdir .cache` — the same shape as the tool source that wrote `.serena` and failed a round — runs inside the sealed worktree, where the cleared write bits refuse it, and if the bits were cleared back the comparison at internal/reviewer/supervise.go:118-119 fails the round on the difference. So two of the three mechanisms README.md:139 names ("it cannot take the third") do bound exactly this write, while line 140 tells a reader on a managed machine that nothing socrates holds bounds it. The accurate form is already in the normative spec (openspec/specs/agent-seam/spec.md:66, "outside the snapshot worktree nothing socrates holds bounds it") and in the design (design.md:44); the same overreaching claim is also in docs/gotchas.md:66 ("runs outside the snapshot worktree where nothing socrates holds bounds it"). What is genuinely uncovered is where the hook's command reaches outside the worktree, not the hook running at all.

The enumeration of what the vendor's help says `--safe-mode` disables is now missing three of its items, and two of the missing ones are precisely what the next sentences present as the residual. The published help reads: "CLAUDE.md, skills, plugins, hooks, MCP servers, custom commands and agents, output styles, workflows, custom themes, custom keybindings, status line and file-suggestion commands, LSP servers, and auto memory do not load". Line 61 drops "status line and file-suggestion commands", "LSP servers" and "auto memory". Line 64 then says "the residual is a hook an administrator's policy configures, along with the status line and the file-suggestion commands" — with the disable list silent about them, that reads as "a status line survives the flag", when the vendor's own sentence is narrower: "Managed settings policy still applies, including policy-configured hooks, status line, and file-suggestion commands". Only the policy-configured ones survive; the machine's own do not load. Dropping "LSP servers" is the same class of gap as the one round 2 f3 fixed for external tool sources, and it is odd beside line 67, whose measurement names the plugin-contributed `LSP` tool. Restore the missing items to line 61 and qualify line 64's status line and file-suggestion commands as policy-configured.

"Managed plugins and policy-configured tool sources are not in that set: those do not load, which socrates measured on such a machine" still attributes to measurement slightly more than the record holds, for the managed-plugin half. The only recorded measurement is the table at openspec/changes/no-customisations-reach-the-reviewer/design.md:32-36 and docs/gotchas.md:67: four external sources went to none and one plugin-contributed `LSP` tool left the tool list. The tool list does not say which source contributed a tool (docs/gotchas.md:88 says the `plugins` field is an inventory of the machine, not a statement about the session), so nothing recorded distinguishes a managed plugin from one the user installed. The claim itself is correct against the vendor's documentation, which says managed plugins do not load; it is the "measured" label that covers policy-configured tool sources and a plugin rather than a managed plugin. Same attribution at AGENTS.md:98, docs/gotchas.md:64 and design.md:44. Round 1 f2 was answered by splitting measurement from documentation, and this is the part of the split the record does not quite carry.

The rewritten requirement names one honest limit of the tool list (a source that connects after the opening event, line 74) and still leaves the silent one unstated and unhandled: an opening event carrying no `tools` field at all. internal/agent/stream.go:93 assigns whatever the init event held, and internal/agent/claude.go:110-120 returns no unexpected tools for an empty list, so a vendor release that stops emitting `tools` turns "The mechanism SHALL NOT be trusted to have worked" into a check that passes on absence of evidence, recording no event for anybody to look at. The suite knows the distinction matters — internal/agent/claude_test.go:80-82 fatals with "the session reported no tools at all, so this test would pass on an empty reading" — which is exactly the case production code does not make. The code is untouched by this change; it is the requirement being rewritten around it that makes the omission worth naming a third time (recorded in both prior rounds with no response).

The design still opens the decision with "The vendor documents it as disabling all customisations", followed by the pre-correction list ("memory files, skills, plugins, hooks, custom commands and agents, output styles, and external tool sources"), seventeen lines above the carve-out added at line 44. Round 2 f4 flagged the unqualified claims in the change's own record; proposal.md:16 and design.md:7 were qualified, this one was not, and it now contradicts both design.md:44 and docs/gotchas.md:61 within the change that is about to be archived, which is where a later reader goes for the reasoning.

The invariant states the residual before the backstop and so keeps the reading order that round 1 f1 had corrected in the README: "What it does not reach is a hook an administrator's policy configures ... it contributes no tool, so the tool list cannot see it either" is followed by "The mechanism is not trusted: socrates reads the session's tool list ... so one check covers every source rather than the one it was written for". A reader on a managed machine reaches "one check covers every source" after being told the check cannot see the one thing that survived. It is defensible if "source" means source of tools, and the README now says plainly that the tool list is not what would catch a policy hook; the invariant leaves it to inference.

risk_rationale: The change is documentation only and the invocation, the tool-list check and the promotion and corpus gates all match what the rewritten specification now says, but the user-facing README states the newly-admitted residual as escaping the seal when the code puts the hook's command inside the sealed worktree, which misdescribes a security property in the direction of claiming less protection than exists.
